Applying AI to cybersecurity, and developing secure and trustworthy AI systems.

![Dark-background diagram of an embedding space. A cluster of blue benign network nodes sits in one region and a cluster of red attack nodes sits in another. A dashed detector boundary separates them, and orange arrows show attack samples disguised as benign ones, crossing the boundary.](../images/research/cyber-hero-graphic.png){width=63% fig-align="center"}

_Figure: Semantic mimicry: attacks disguised in the language of normal behavior cross a detector boundary designed to separate benign from malicious samples._

## Research Topics

- Zero-day and zero-shot threat detection
- Network intrusion detection
- Semantic threat representation
- Generative AI for cybersecurity
- LLM security and AI red teaming
- RAG and GraphRAG
- Trustworthy and secure generative AI

## Key Research Questions

- How can intrusion detection identify attack classes never seen during training?
- How can LLM-based systems be evaluated for safety failures through automated red teaming?
